mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which historically precedes either wage inflation or policy tightening, both of which compress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in the 10-year Treasury yield (not available in catalog, so use RSAFS as proxy for savings/investment climate) signals a shift toward risk-off sentiment, which reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND RSAFS falls month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200k for five consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which supports corporate profit margins and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 4%).
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 5 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL <= 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes with CPIAUCSL <= 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.4% for three consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side recovery, which boosts earnings for industrial firms and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
